Middle East.headline: Yemen / Saudi Arabia — Cross-border missile attacks and escalating domestic fighting
Middle East.body: Saudi Arabia intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles targeting several domestic regions, including Mecca, prompting France to pledge military assets to protect the Yanbu oil terminal. The cross-border escalation coincides with renewed fighting in Yemen that has killed dozens of people. UNICEF reported that the intensifying conflict is driving fresh displacement and worsening severe hunger and child malnutrition, placing heavy pressure on emergency displacement facilities such as Aden's Al Firdous center.

Middle East.headline: Occupied Palestinian Territory — Vehicle attack critically injures Israeli reservist in West Bank
Middle East.body: An Israeli military reservist was critically injured in a car-ramming attack at a security checkpoint near the Beit Horon settlement in the occupied West Bank. Israeli forces present at the scene opened fire on the Palestinian driver following the incident.

Middle East.headline: Gaza Strip / Israel — Rights group alleges systematic blockade of basic supplies
Middle East.body: A human rights organization published an investigation alleging that senior commanders of Israel's COGAT military unit directed a government-sanctioned blockade restricting food, water, fuel, and medical supplies from entering the Gaza Strip between October 2023 and mid-2026. The report asserts that administrative restrictions on humanitarian aid created severe food insecurity and extreme physical suffering across the enclave.

Americas.headline: Mexico / United States — Category 5 Hurricane Polo threatens southwestern coast as Hurricane Nolo targets Hawaii
Americas.body: Hurricane Polo has intensified back into a Category 5 storm off southwestern Mexico, bringing severe rainfall and flood risks to coastal regions. The U.S. National Hurricane Center reported maximum sustained winds of 160 mph, with the core positioned about 250 miles south-southwest of Cabo Corrientes. Fluctuations in intensity are expected over 12 to 24 hours before weakening begins. Concurrently, Hurricane Nolo is tracking toward Hawaii's Big Island, representing the state's third hurricane threat of the year.

Americas.headline: United States — Government pledges $267 million in additional health assistance to combat Ebola outbreak
Americas.body: The United States State Department has pledged an additional $267 million in funding to help contain a fast-spreading Ebola outbreak. The allocation supplements $887 million previously provided by the U.S. government. According to official statements, the new funding will support the construction of treatment units, safe burial practices, and expanded containment programs aimed at stopping further transmission.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — Protection, education, and health risks persist three months after major earthquakes
Americas.body: Humanitarian organisations report sustained risks to child protection, education, and health services three months after destructive earthquakes hit Venezuela in June. Lingering physical and psychological impacts continue to affect local populations. Aid workers operating between Valencia and Caracas note that lingering infrastructural damage and quiet aftershocks present long-term challenges for displaced communities struggling to rebuild.

Africa.headline: DRC — Ebola Outbreak Surges Amid Strain Mismatch and Insecurity
Africa.body: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading beyond its epicentre, driven by a strain-vaccine mismatch, insecurity, and community mistrust. While infections decreased in Ituri province, North Kivu registered a 73 percent surge in cases over three weeks, and a doctor died in Kisangani. The World Health Organization warned the outbreak could become the deadliest on record. To support response efforts, the United States pledged an additional $267 million in humanitarian assistance, bringing its total contribution for this outbreak to $887 million.

Africa.headline: Somalia — Anticipated El Niño Floods Threaten Millions with Acute Hunger
Africa.body: The United Nations and Somali authorities warned that anticipated El Niño flooding between October and December will severely aggravate hunger and child malnutrition. Latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification data projects that 5.4 million people will face crisis levels of food insecurity or worse, with 1.5 million reaching emergency levels. Additionally, 1.92 million children under five will require treatment for malnutrition, including 433,000 children affected by severe acute malnutrition.

Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: US releases additional US$267mil to combat Ebola outbreak
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: “To date, the United States government has provided US$887 million in direct health and humanitarian assistance to combat the Ebola outbreak,” the US state department said in a statement, adding that Washington was the largest aid provider for the latest outbreak.
